title.zh: 卷一百五十六 列傳第八十一 楊戴陽二李韓杜邢
title.en: Volume 156 Biographies 81: Yang, Dai, Yang, Two Li's, Han, Du, Xing
title.raw: 卷一百五十六 列傳第八十一 楊戴陽二李韓杜邢 Volume 156 Biographies 81: Yang, Dai, Yang, Two Li's, Han, Du, Xing

sentences.zh: 楊戴陽二李韓杜邢

translations.literal: Yang, Dai, Yang, two Lis, Han, Du, and Xing
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chaocheng; Dai Xiuyan; Yang Huiyuan; the two Lis; Han; Du; and Xing

sentences.zh: 楊朝晟

translations.literal: Yang Chaocheng
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chaocheng

sentences.zh: 楊朝晟，字叔明，夏州朔方人。

translations.literal: Yang Chaocheng, styled Shuming, was a native of Shuofang in Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chaocheng, whose style name was Shuming, came from Shuofang in Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 興行間，以先鋒功授甘泉府果毅。

translations.literal: During the Xingyuan era, for merit as vanguard he was appointed a guoyi officer of Ganquan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xingyuan reign he was made a guoyi officer of Ganquan Prefecture for his service in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 建中初，從李懷光討劉文喜涇州，斬獲多，加驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: In the early Jianzhong period he followed Li Huai'guang in the campaign against Liu Wenxi at Jing Prefecture, took many heads and captives, and was promoted to General of Fast Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong era he followed Li Huai'guang against Liu Wenxi at Jingzhou, winning many kills and captures, and was promoted to General of Fast Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 李納寇徐州，從唐朝臣往討，常冠軍。

translations.literal: When Li Na raided Xuzhou, he followed Tang Chaochen to attack and often led the army in victory.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Na raided Xuzhou, he marched with Tang Chaochen to suppress him and repeatedly led the army to victory.

sentences.zh: 懷光赴難奉天，屬朝晟兵千人下咸陽，賜實封百五十戶。

translations.literal: When Huai'guang marched to relieve Fengtian, Chaocheng was assigned a thousand men to advance on Xianyang and was granted a substantive fief of one hundred fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'guang went to relieve Fengtian, Chaocheng was given a thousand troops to advance on Xianyang and was granted a substantive fief of one hundred fifty households.

sentences.zh: 懷光反，韓遊瑰退保邠、寧，賊黨張昕守邠州，大索軍實，多募士，欲潛歸之。

translations.literal: When Huai'guang rebelled, Han Yougui withdrew to hold Bin and Ning; the rebel partisan Zhang Xin garrisoned Bin Prefecture, extensively seized military supplies, recruited many troops, and intended to go over to the rebels in secret.
translations.idiomatic: After Huai'guang rebelled, Han Yougui fell back to defend Bin and Ning. The rebel partisan Zhang Xin held Bin Prefecture, stripped the stores, recruited troops widely, and planned to defect to Huai'guang in secret.

sentences.zh: 朝晟父懷賓為遊瑰將，夜以數十騎斬昕及同謀者。

translations.literal: Chaocheng's father Huaibin served as Han Yougui's officer; by night he led several dozen horsemen and slew Zhang Xin along with his fellow conspirators.
translations.idiomatic: Chaocheng's father Huaibin was one of Yougui's officers. By night he led several dozen horsemen and cut down Zhang Xin and his fellow plotters.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰遣懷賓告行在，德宗勞問，授兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Yougui sent Huaibin to report to the traveling court; Emperor Dezong received him with praise and appointed him concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui sent Huaibin to report to the traveling court. Emperor Dezong received him with commendation and appointed him concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 朝晟泣見懷光曰：「父立功於國，子當誅，不可以主兵。」

translations.literal: Chaocheng came weeping before Huai'guang and said: "My father has done merit for the state, while I as his son deserve death. I cannot be allowed to command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chaocheng came weeping before Huai'guang and said, "My father has won merit for the state, yet I as his son deserve death. I ought not be allowed to command troops.

sentences.zh: 懷光縶之。

translations.literal: Huai'guang had him bound.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang had him bound.

sentences.zh: 及諸軍圍河中，遊瑰營長春宮，而懷賓戰甚力。

translations.literal: When the allied armies besieged Hezhong, Yougui encamped at Changchun Palace, and Huaibin fought with exceptional vigor.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies besieged Hezhong, Yougui encamped at Changchun Palace while Huaibin fought with exceptional vigor.

sentences.zh: 懷光平，帝原朝晟，因為遊瑰都虞候。

translations.literal: After Huai'guang was suppressed, the emperor pardoned Chaocheng and made him chief adjutant under Yougui.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huai'guang was defeated, the emperor pardoned Chaocheng and appointed him chief adjutant under Yougui.

sentences.zh: 父子皆開府、賓客、御史中丞，軍中以為榮。

translations.literal: Father and son both held the titles of unequal Sixteen Guards general, guest of the Privy Council, and vice censor-in-chief — an honor celebrated throughout the army.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son alike held the ranks of honorary Sixteen Guards general, Privy Council guest, and vice censor-in-chief — a distinction the army regarded with pride.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃犯邊，遊瑰自將守寧州，而禦士寬，軍驕。

translations.literal: When Tibetans raided the frontier, Yougui took the field in person to hold Ningzhou, but his treatment of the troops was indulgent and the army grew arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans raided the border, Yougui took command in person to hold Ningzhou, but his discipline was lax and the army grew insubordinate.

sentences.zh: 及張獻甫來代，軍遂亂，朝晟逃於郊。

translations.literal: When Zhang Xianfu arrived to succeed him, the army promptly mutinied; Chaocheng fled into the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xianfu arrived to replace him, the army mutinied at once; Chaocheng fled into the countryside.

sentences.zh: 眾脅監軍，請以范希朝為節度使。

translations.literal: The mutineers coerced the army supervisor and demanded that Fan Xichao be made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The troops coerced the army supervisor and demanded that Fan Xichao be made military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 希朝時已在京師。

translations.literal: Xichao was then already at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xichao was already at the capital.

sentences.zh: 明日，朝晟出，紿眾曰：「予來賀所請之當也。」

translations.literal: The next day Chaocheng appeared and deceived the troops, saying: "I have come to congratulate you — what you requested was exactly right.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Chaocheng came forward and deceived the crowd, saying, "I have come to congratulate you — what you asked for was exactly right.

sentences.zh: 眾稍定。

translations.literal: At that the crowd calmed somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: At that the crowd calmed somewhat.

sentences.zh: 朝晟結諸將謀誅首惡者。

translations.literal: Chaocheng joined the other generals in a plot to kill the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Chaocheng joined the other generals in a plot to execute the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 居三日，紿遣人自邠來，曰：「前請報罷，張公已舍邠矣，反者皆當死，吾不願盡誅也，第取首惡者。」

translations.literal: After three days he sent a man from Bin as another deception, saying: "The prior petition has been rejected. Lord Zhang has already departed from Bin. All who rebelled deserve death, but I do not mean to execute everyone — only the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he staged another deception, sending a man from Bin who said, "Your earlier petition has been denied. Lord Zhang has already left Bin. All who rebelled deserve death, but I do not wish to kill everyone — only the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 眾所讙指，斬二百餘人，獻甫遂入於軍。

translations.literal: Those whom the crowd eagerly singled out were beheaded — more than two hundred men — and Xianfu then took command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Those whom the crowd eagerly pointed out were beheaded — more than two hundred men — and Xianfu then took command of the army.

sentences.zh: 帝以希朝為節度副使，而朝晟加御史大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Xichao deputy military commissioner and promoted Chaocheng to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Xichao deputy military commissioner and promoted Chaocheng to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 貞元九年，城鹽州，發卒護境，朝晟屯木波堡。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenyuan they fortified Yazhou and sent troops to guard the frontier; Chaocheng encamped at Fort Mubo.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenyuan the court fortified Yazhou and sent troops to guard the frontier; Chaocheng encamped at Fort Mubo.

sentences.zh: 會獻甫卒，有詔代為邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: When Xianfu died, an edict named Chaocheng military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianfu died, an edict appointed Chaocheng military commissioner of Binning.

sentences.zh: 朝晟請城方渠，合道，木波以遏吐蕃路。

translations.literal: Chaocheng asked to build fortified posts at Fangqu, Hedao, and Mubo to block the Tibetan advance.
translations.idiomatic: Chaocheng requested fortifications at Fangqu, Hedao, and Mubo to block the Tibetan route.

sentences.zh: 詔問：「須兵幾何？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "How many troops will be required?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "How many troops will be needed?

sentences.zh: 報曰：「部兵可辦。」

translations.literal: He replied: "My division's troops can manage it."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "My division's troops can handle it."

sentences.zh: 帝問：「前日城五原，興師七萬，今何易邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "When we fortified Wuyuan before, we mobilized seventy thousand men. Why is this so easy now?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "When we fortified Wuyuan before, we raised an army of seventy thousand. Why is this so easy now?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「鹽州之役，虜先知之。

translations.literal: He answered: "In the Yazhou campaign the enemy learned of it in advance.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "In the Yazhou campaign the enemy learned of our plans in advance.

sentences.zh: 今薄戎而城，虜料王師不十萬，勢難輕入。

translations.literal: Now we build close to the enemy border. The barbarians reckon the imperial forces at fewer than a hundred thousand and will hardly dare a light incursion.
translations.idiomatic: Now we build close to the enemy camps. The barbarians estimate the imperial army at fewer than a hundred thousand and will hardly dare a light raid.

sentences.zh: 若發部兵，十日至塞下，未三旬城畢，積芻聚糧，留卒守之，寇至不可拔，萊野翦夷，虜且走，此萬全計也。

translations.literal: If we send only my division, they will reach the frontier in ten days and finish the walls within thirty. We can stock fodder and grain and leave troops to garrison the place; when the enemy comes they cannot take it, their pastures and fields will be laid waste, and they will have to withdraw. This is a plan without flaw.
translations.idiomatic: If we send only my division, they will reach the frontier in ten days and finish the walls within thirty. We can stock fodder and grain and leave troops to hold the place; when the enemy comes they cannot take it, their pastures and fields will be laid waste, and they will withdraw. This is a plan without flaw.

sentences.zh: 若大發兵，閱月乃至，虜亦來，來必戰，戰則不暇城矣。」

translations.literal: If we mobilize a great host, it will take a month to arrive; the enemy will come too, and coming they will force a battle — and in battle there will be no time to build the walls."
translations.idiomatic: If we mobilize a great host, it will take a month to arrive; the enemy will come as well, and when they come there must be battle — and in battle there will be no time to build the walls."

sentences.zh: 帝納其策。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his plan.

sentences.zh: 師次方渠，水乏。

translations.literal: When the army reached Fangqu, water was scarce.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Fangqu, water ran short.

sentences.zh: 有青蛇降險下走，視其跡，水從而流，朝晟使築防環之，遂為渟淵，士飲仰足，圖其事以聞。

translations.literal: A green serpent came down a steep slope; where it passed, water flowed forth. Chaocheng had an embankment built around the spot until it formed a deep pool, and the troops drank their fill. He had the event recorded and reported to court.
translations.idiomatic: A green serpent came down a steep slope; where it passed, water followed. Chaocheng had an embankment built around the spot until it formed a deep pool, and the troops drank their fill. He had the event illustrated and reported to court.

sentences.zh: 有詔置祠，命泉曰應聖。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a shrine erected and named the spring "Responsive to the Sage."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a shrine built and named the spring "Responsive to the Sage."

sentences.zh: 已城，吐蕃悉眾至，度不能害，乃引去。

translations.literal: When the fortifications were finished, the Tibetans marched out in full strength; seeing they could do no harm, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Once the walls were finished, the Tibetans came in full force; seeing they could do no harm, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 復城馬嶺而歸，開地三百里。

translations.literal: He then fortified Malin as well and returned, extending the frontier three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He then fortified Malin as well and returned, opening three hundred li of new territory.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒於屯。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan he died at his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan he died at his garrison post.

sentences.zh: 戴休顏 弟戴休璿 戴休晏

translations.literal: Dai Xiuyan; his younger brothers Dai Xiuxuan and Dai Xiuyan
translations.idiomatic: Dai Xiuyan; his younger brothers Dai Xiuxuan and Dai Xiuyan

sentences.zh: 戴休顏，字休顏，夏州人。

translations.literal: Dai Xiuyan, styled Xiuyan, was a native of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Xiuyan — his style name was also Xiuyan — was a native of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 家世尚武，誌膽不常。

translations.literal: His family had long honored the military arts, and his ambition and courage were out of the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long honored the military arts, and his ambition and courage were extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀引為大將，諭平党項羌，以安河曲。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi took him on as a senior officer and had him subdue the Tangut Qiang to secure the Hequ region.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi took him on as a senior officer and had him pacify the Tangut Qiang to secure the Hequ region.

sentences.zh: 試太常卿，封濟陰郡公，進封咸寧郡王，兼朔方節度副使。

translations.literal: He was made acting Grand Master of Ceremonies, enfeoffed as Duke of Jiyin, then advanced to Prince of Xianning, and appointed concurrent deputy commissioner of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Grand Master of Ceremonies, enfeoffed Duke of Jiyin, then advanced to Prince of Xianning, and appointed concurrent deputy commissioner of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 城邠州功最，遷鹽州刺史。

translations.literal: For outstanding merit in fortifying Bin Prefecture he was transferred to prefect of Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: For the greatest merit in fortifying Bin Prefecture he was transferred to prefect of Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 朱泚反，率兵三千晝夜馳，奔問行在，德宗嘉之，賜實戶二百。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he led three thousand men in forced marches day and night to reach the traveling court; Dezong commended him and granted a substantive fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he led three thousand men in forced marches day and night to reach the traveling court. Dezong commended him and granted a substantive fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 與渾瑊、杜希全、韓遊瑰等扞禦有勞。

translations.literal: Together with Hun Jian, Du Xiquan, Han Yougui, and others he did distinguished service in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Hun Jian, Du Xiquan, Han Yougui, and others he rendered distinguished service in the defense.

sentences.zh: 帝進狩梁、洋，留守奉天。

translations.literal: When the emperor withdrew toward Liang and Yang, he remained to hold Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew toward Liang and Yang, he remained to hold Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 李懷光屯咸陽，使人誘之，休顏斬其使，勒兵自守。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang, encamped at Xianyang, sent men to win him over; Xiuyan beheaded the envoy and rallied his troops to hold fast.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai'guang, encamped at Xianyang, sent men to win him over. Xiuyan beheaded the envoy and rallied his troops to hold firm.

sentences.zh: 懷光眙駭，自涇陽夜走。

translations.literal: Huai'guang was struck dumb with fear and fled by night from Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang was struck with terror and fled by night from Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校工部尚書、奉天行營節度使。

translations.literal: He was made acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of the Fengtian field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of the Fengtian field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 合渾瑊兵破泚偏師，斬首三千級，追至中渭橋。

translations.literal: Joining with Hun Jian's forces he routed Zhu Ci's detached column, took three thousand heads, and pursued as far as the Central Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Joining Hun Jian's forces he routed Zhu Ci's detached column, took three thousand heads, and pursued as far as the Central Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 京師平，又與瑊率兵趨岐陽，邀泚殘黨。

translations.literal: After the capital was recovered, he again led troops with Jian toward Qiyang to cut off Zhu Ci's remaining followers.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was recovered, he again led troops with Jian toward Qiyang to intercept Zhu Ci's remaining followers.

sentences.zh: 加檢校尚書右僕射，進戶四百。

translations.literal: He was made acting Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat and his fief was increased by four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat and his fief was increased by four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 從乘輿至京師，賜女樂、甲第，拜左龍武軍統軍。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial carriage back to the capital, was granted female musicians and a grand residence, and was appointed commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the imperial carriage back to the capital, was granted female musicians and a grand residence, and was appointed commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 弟休璿，歷開府儀同三司，封東陽郡王；

translations.literal: His younger brother Xiuxuan rose through the ranks to Honored Companion of the First Rank and was enfeoffed Prince of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiuxuan rose to Honored Companion of the First Rank and was enfeoffed Prince of Dongyang;

sentences.zh: 休晏，歷輔國大將軍，封彭城郡公。

translations.literal: Xiuyan rose to Supporting-the-State Grand General and was enfeoffed Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyan rose to Supporting-the-State Grand General and was enfeoffed Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 俱以將略稱。

translations.literal: Both were famed for their military ability.
translations.idiomatic: Both were famed for their military ability.

sentences.zh: 陽惠元

translations.literal: Yang Huiyuan
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huiyuan

sentences.zh: 陽惠元，平州人。

translations.literal: Yang Huiyuan was a native of Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huiyuan was a native of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以趫勇奮，事平盧軍。

translations.literal: For his bounding courage he served in the Pinglu army.
translations.idiomatic: For his bounding courage he served in the Pinglu army.

sentences.zh: 從田神功、李忠臣浮海入青州。

translations.literal: He followed Tian Shenggong and Li Zhongchen in crossing the sea to enter Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Tian Shenggong and Li Zhongchen in crossing the sea to enter Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔以兵隸神策，為京西兵馬使，鎮奉天。

translations.literal: By edict his troops were placed under the Shence armies; he was made commissioner of Jingxi army and horse and garrisoned Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: By edict his troops were placed under the Shence armies; he was made commissioner of Jingxi army and horse and garrisoned Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 德宗初立，稍繩諸節度跋扈者。

translations.literal: When Dezong first took the throne, he began to restrain the overbearing military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong first took the throne, he began to rein in the overbearing military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 於是李正己屯曹州，田悅增河上兵，河南大擾。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Zhengyi encamped at Caozhou and Tian Yue reinforced his troops along the Yellow River; Henan was thrown into great turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Li Zhengyi encamped at Caozhou and Tian Yue reinforced his troops along the Yellow River; Henan was thrown into great turmoil.

sentences.zh: 詔移兵萬二千戍關東，帝御望春樓誓師，因勞遣諸將。

translations.literal: An edict ordered twelve thousand two hundred troops to garrison east of the pass; the emperor reviewed them at Wangchun Tower, took the oath of the army, and thereupon saw off the generals with words of encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered twelve thousand two hundred troops to garrison east of the pass. The emperor reviewed them at Wangchun Tower, took the army's oath, and thereupon saw off the generals with words of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 酒至神策，將士不敢飲。

translations.literal: When wine was offered to the Shence troops, the officers and men dared not drink.
translations.idiomatic: When wine was offered to the Shence troops, the officers and men dared not drink.

sentences.zh: 帝問故，惠元曰：「初發奉天，臣之帥張巨濟與眾約：『是役也，不立功，毋飲酒！』

translations.literal: The emperor asked why; Huiyuan said: "When we first set out from Fengtian, my commander Zhang Juji made this pledge with the men: 'In this campaign, unless we achieve merit, we shall not drink wine!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why. Huiyuan said, "When we first set out from Fengtian, my commander Zhang Juji pledged with the men: 'In this campaign, unless we win merit, we shall not drink wine!

sentences.zh: 臣不敢食其言。」

translations.literal: I dare not go back on his word.'
translations.idiomatic: I dare not go back on his word.'

sentences.zh: 既行，有饋於道，惟惠元軍瓶罍不發。

translations.literal: On the march, provisions were offered along the way, but only Huiyuan's army left its jars and bottles unopened.
translations.idiomatic: On the march, provisions were offered along the way, but only Huiyuan's army left its jars and bottles unopened.

sentences.zh: 帝咨嘆不已，璽書慰勞。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled repeatedly and sent an imperial letter of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled repeatedly and sent an imperial letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 俄以兵三千會諸將擊田悅，戰御河，奪三橋，惠元功多。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he brought three thousand men to join the other generals against Tian Yue, fought at the Yu River, captured three bridges, and Huiyuan's merit was among the highest.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he brought three thousand men to join the other generals against Tian Yue, fought at the Yu River, captured three bridges, and Huiyuan's merit ranked among the highest.

sentences.zh: 以兵屬李懷光。

translations.literal: His troops were placed under Li Huai'guang's command.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were placed under Li Huai'guang's command.

sentences.zh: 及朱泚反，自河朔赴難，解奉天圍，加檢校工部尚書，攝貝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he marched from Hebei to the emperor's relief, broke the siege of Fengtian, was made acting Minister of Works, and held Beizhou as acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he marched from Hebei to relieve the emperor, broke the siege of Fengtian, was made acting Minister of Works, and held Beizhou as acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 詔惠元與神策行營節度使李晟、鄜坊節度使李建徽及懷光聯營便橋。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Huiyuan to join camps with Li Sheng, commissioner of the Shence campaign, Li Jianhui of Fufang, and Huai'guang at Bian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Huiyuan to camp jointly with Li Sheng, commissioner of the Shence campaign, Li Jianhui of Fufang, and Huai'guang at Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 晟知懷光且叛，移屯東渭橋。

translations.literal: Sheng, knowing Huai'guang was on the verge of rebellion, shifted his camp to the East Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, knowing Huai'guang was about to rebel, shifted his camp to the East Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士陸贄諫帝曰：「四將接壘，晟等兵寡位下，為懷光所易，勢不兩完。

translations.literal: The Hanlin academician Lu Zhi admonished the emperor: "With four generals camped side by side, Sheng and the others have few troops and lower rank; Huai'guang can easily dominate them — the situation cannot end well for both sides.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin academician Lu Zhi admonished the emperor: "With four generals camped side by side, Sheng and the others have few troops and lower rank. Huai'guang can easily overpower them — the situation cannot end well for both sides.

sentences.zh: 晟既慮變，請與惠元東徙，則建徽孤立。

translations.literal: Sheng already fears trouble and asks to move east with Huiyuan; then Jianhui would stand alone.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng already fears trouble and asks to move east with Huiyuan; then Jianhui would stand alone.

sentences.zh: 宜因晟行，合兩軍皆往，以備賊為解，趣裝進道，則懷光計無所施。」

translations.literal: You should use Sheng's move as the occasion, send both armies east together under the pretext of guarding against the rebels, have them pack and march at once — then Huai'guang's scheme will have no opening.
translations.idiomatic: You should use Sheng's move as the occasion, send both armies east together under the pretext of guarding against the rebels, have them pack and march at once — then Huai'guang's scheme will have no opening.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，使神策將李升往伺。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed this and sent the Shence officer Li Sheng to reconnoiter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed this and sent the Shence officer Li Sheng to reconnoiter.

sentences.zh: 還奏：「懷光反明甚。」

translations.literal: On his return he reported: "Huai'guang's rebellion is altogether clear.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported, "Huai'guang's rebellion is altogether clear.

sentences.zh: 是夕，奪二軍，惠元、建徽走奉天，懷光遣將冉宗馳騎追及於好畤。

translations.literal: That same night Huai'guang seized the two armies; Huiyuan and Jianhui fled to Fengtian. Huai'guang sent the general Ran Zong in pursuit and overtook them at Haozhi.
translations.idiomatic: That same night Huai'guang seized the two armies. Huiyuan and Jianhui fled to Fengtian. Huai'guang sent the general Ran Zong in pursuit and overtook them at Haozhi.

sentences.zh: 惠元被髮呼天，血流出眥，袒裼戰而死。

translations.literal: Huiyuan tore his hair and cried to heaven, blood streaming from the corners of his eyes; stripping to the waist he fought and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyuan tore his hair and cried to heaven, blood streaming from the corners of his eyes. Stripping to the waist, he fought and was killed.

sentences.zh: 二子晟、暠匿井中，皆及害。

translations.literal: His two sons Sheng and Gao hid in a well but were found and killed.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons Sheng and Gao hid in a well but were found and killed.

sentences.zh: 建徽獨免。

translations.literal: Only Jianhui escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Only Jianhui escaped.

sentences.zh: 詔贈惠元尚書左僕射，晟殿中監，暠邠州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made Huiyuan Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Sheng palace director, and Gao prefect of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made Huiyuan Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Sheng palace director, and Gao prefect of Bin.

sentences.zh: 少子旻，字公素。

translations.literal: His youngest son Min, styled Gongsu,
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Min, styled Gongsu,

sentences.zh: 惠元之死，被八創，墮別井，或救得免。

translations.literal: at his father's death suffered eight wounds and fell into another well, but someone pulled him out alive.
translations.idiomatic: when his father died suffered eight wounds and fell into another well, but someone pulled him out alive.

sentences.zh: 歷邢州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 盧從史既縛，潞軍潰，有驍卒五千，從史嘗以子視者，奔於旻，旻閉城不內。

translations.literal: After Lu Congshi was captured, the Lu army collapsed; five thousand crack troops whom Congshi had treated like sons fled to Min, but Min shut the gates and would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Congshi was captured, the Lu army collapsed. Five thousand crack troops whom Congshi had treated like sons fled to Min, but Min shut the gates and would not admit them.

sentences.zh: 眾皆哭曰：「奴失帥，今公有完城，又度支錢百萬在府，少賜之，為表天子求旌節。」

translations.literal: They all wept and said: "We have lost our commander. You hold a secure city, and a million strings of Treasury funds lie in your prefectural office — grant us a little and memorialize the Son of Heaven to obtain a military commission for us.
translations.idiomatic: They all wept and said, "We have lost our commander. You hold a secure city, and a million strings of Treasury funds lie in your prefectural office — grant us a little and memorialize the Son of Heaven to obtain a military commission for us.

sentences.zh: 旻開諭禍福遣之，眾感悟，遂還軍。

translations.literal: Min opened the gates, explained the consequences to them, and sent them away; the men came to their senses and returned to their units.
translations.idiomatic: Min opened the gates, explained the consequences to them, and sent them away. The men came to their senses and returned to their units.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嘉之，遷易州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong commended him and transferred him to prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong commended him and transferred him to prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 王師討吳元濟，以唐州刺史提兵深入二百里，薄申州，拔外郛，殘其垣。

translations.literal: When the imperial armies attacked Wu Yuanji, as prefect of Tangzhou he led troops two hundred li into enemy territory, pressed Shenzhou, took the outer suburbs, and destroyed its walls.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial armies attacked Wu Yuanji, as prefect of Tangzhou he led troops two hundred li into enemy territory, pressed Shenzhou, took the outer suburbs, and destroyed its walls.

sentences.zh: 以功加御史中丞。

translations.literal: For this merit he was made vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For this merit he was made vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 容州西原蠻反，授本州經略招討使，擊定之。

translations.literal: When the Xiyuan tribes of Rongzhou rebelled, he was appointed pacification and punitive commissioner for the prefecture and suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiyuan tribes of Rongzhou rebelled, he was appointed pacification and punitive commissioner for the prefecture and suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 進御史大夫，合邕、容兩管為一道。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and merged the Yong and Rong circuits into a single command.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and merged the Yong and Rong circuits into a single command.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 李元諒

translations.literal: Li Yuanliang
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanliang

sentences.zh: 李元諒，安息人。

translations.literal: Li Yuanliang was a man of Parthian (Anxi) descent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanliang was of Parthian descent.

sentences.zh: 本安氏，少為宦官駱奉先養息，冒姓駱，名元光。

translations.literal: His original surname was An. As a youth he was adopted by the eunuch Luo Fengxian, took the surname Luo in pretense, and was named Yuanguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally of the An clan. As a youth he was adopted by the eunuch Luo Fengxian, took the surname Luo falsely, and was named Yuanguang.

sentences.zh: 美須髯，鷙敢有謀。

translations.literal: He had a fine beard, was fierce and bold, and possessed stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He had a fine beard, was fierce and bold, and possessed stratagems.

sentences.zh: 以宿衛積勞試太子詹事。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit in palace guard service he was made acting Administrator of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merit in palace guard service he was made acting Administrator of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 李懷讓節度鎮國，署奏以自副。

translations.literal: When Li Huairang was military commissioner of Zhenguo, he appointed him to his staff as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huairang was military commissioner of Zhenguo, he appointed him to his staff as deputy.

sentences.zh: 居軍十年，士心憚服。

translations.literal: He remained with the army ten years, and the troops feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He remained with the army ten years, and the troops feared and submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 德宗出奉天，賊遣將何望之襲華州，於是刺史董晉棄城走。

translations.literal: When Dezong left Fengtian, the rebels sent the general He Wangzhi to raid Huazhou; the prefect Dong Jin thereupon abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong left Fengtian, the rebels sent the general He Wangzhi to raid Huazhou. The prefect Dong Jin thereupon abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 望之欲聚兵以絕東道，元諒自潼關引兵徑薄其城，拔之。

translations.literal: Wangzhi wished to gather troops to cut the eastern route; Yuanliang led troops from Tong Pass straight against the city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi wished to gather troops to cut the eastern route. Yuanliang led troops from Tong Pass straight against the city and took it.

sentences.zh: 時兵興倉卒，裹罽為鎧，剡蒿為矢，募兵數日至萬餘，軍氣乃振。

translations.literal: War had arisen in haste; they wrapped felt as armor and carved artemisia as arrows. Within days recruited troops reached more than ten thousand, and army morale revived.
translations.idiomatic: War had arisen in haste. They wrapped felt as armor and carved artemisia as arrows. Within days recruited troops reached more than ten thousand, and army morale revived.

sentences.zh: 賊來攻，輒卻。

translations.literal: When rebels came to attack, they were always repelled.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels came to attack, they were always repelled.

sentences.zh: 時尚可孤守藍田，元諒屯昭應，王權壁中渭橋，賊兵不能逾渭南。

translations.literal: At the time Shang Kegu held Lantian, Yuanliang encamped at Zhaoying, and Wang Quan fortified the Central Wei Bridge; rebel troops could not cross south of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shang Kegu held Lantian, Yuanliang encamped at Zhaoying, and Wang Quan fortified the Central Wei Bridge, so rebel troops could not cross south of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷鎮國軍節度使，封武康郡王。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to military commissioner of the Zhenguo army and enfeoffed Prince of Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made military commissioner of the Zhenguo army and enfeoffed Prince of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔發豳、隴兵東討李希烈。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had dispatched Bin and Long troops east to attack Li Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had dispatched Bin and Long troops east to attack Li Xilie.

sentences.zh: 師方出關，泚使劉忠孝召還；

translations.literal: The army had just left the pass when Zhu Ci sent Liu Zhongxiao to recall them;
translations.idiomatic: The army had just left the pass when Zhu Ci sent Liu Zhongxiao to recall them;

sentences.zh: 至華陰，華陰尉李夷簡說驛官捕之，追及關，元諒斬以徇，所召兵不得入，由是華州獨完。

translations.literal: at Huayin the assistant magistrate Li Yijian persuaded the post station officer to seize him; pursued to the pass, Yuanliang beheaded him as a warning, and the recalled troops could not enter — thus Huazhou alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: At Huayin the assistant magistrate Li Yijian persuaded the post station officer to seize him. Pursued to the pass, Yuanliang beheaded him as a warning, and the recalled troops could not enter — thus Huazhou alone remained intact.

sentences.zh: 俄詔元諒與李晟收京師，次浐西。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered Yuanliang and Li Sheng to recover the capital; they halted west of Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered Yuanliang and Li Sheng to recover the capital. They halted west of Chan.

sentences.zh: 元諒先奮鏖賊，敗之，進屯苑東，晟使壞苑垣入。

translations.literal: Yuanliang first fought fiercely and defeated the rebels, advanced to encamp east of the park, and Sheng had the park wall broken to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang first fought fiercely and defeated the rebels, advanced to encamp east of the imperial park, and Sheng had the park wall broken to enter.

sentences.zh: 泚連戰皆北，遂大潰，京師平。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci was defeated in successive battles and then routed in great disorder; the capital was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci was defeated in successive battles and then routed in great disorder. The capital was pacified.

sentences.zh: 讓功於晟，退壁近郊。

translations.literal: He yielded merit to Sheng and withdrew to fortify the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: He yielded the credit to Sheng and withdrew to fortify the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 加檢校尚書左僕射，實封戶五百，賜甲第、女樂、一子六品官。

translations.literal: He was made acting Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, granted a substantive fief of five hundred households, and bestowed a grand residence, female musicians, and a sixth-rank office for one son.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, granted a substantive fief of five hundred households, and bestowed a grand residence, female musicians, and a sixth-rank office for one son.

sentences.zh: 李懷光反，與馬燧、渾瑊討之。

translations.literal: When Li Huai'guang rebelled, he joined Ma Sui and Hun Jian in suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huai'guang rebelled, he joined Ma Sui and Hun Jian in suppressing him.

sentences.zh: 其將徐廷光素易元諒，數嫚罵，為優胡戲，斥侮其祖。

translations.literal: Huai'guang's officer Xu Tingguang had always looked down on Yuanliang, repeatedly insulted him, staged comic performances mocking him, and reviled his ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang's officer Xu Tingguang had always looked down on Yuanliang, repeatedly insulted him, staged comic performances mocking him, and reviled his ancestors.

sentences.zh: 又使約降，曰：「我降漢將耳。」

translations.literal: He also sent to arrange surrender, saying: "I surrender only to a Han general.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent to arrange surrender, saying, "I surrender only to a Han general.

sentences.zh: 及馬燧至，降於燧。

translations.literal: When Ma Sui arrived, he surrendered to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Sui arrived, he surrendered to Sui.

sentences.zh: 元諒見韓遊瑰曰：「彼詬吾祖，今日斬之，子助我乎？」

translations.literal: Yuanliang saw Han Yougui and said: "He reviled my ancestors — today I shall behead him. Will you help me?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang saw Han Yougui and said, "He reviled my ancestors — today I shall behead him. Will you help me?

sentences.zh: 許諾。

translations.literal: He agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而遇諸道，即數其罪，叱左右斬之，詣燧謝。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he met the various commanders, recounted his crimes, ordered attendants to behead him, and went to Sui to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he met the various commanders, recounted his crimes, ordered attendants to behead him, and went to Sui to apologize.

sentences.zh: 燧大怒，將殺元諒，遊瑰見曰：「殺一偏裨尚爾，即殺一節度，法宜如何？」

translations.literal: Sui was furious and was about to kill Yuanliang. Yougui intervened and said: "If killing a subordinate officer provokes this, what would the law say of killing a military commissioner?
translations.idiomatic: Sui was furious and was about to kill Yuanliang. Yougui intervened and said, "If killing a subordinate officer provokes this, what would the law say of killing a military commissioner?

sentences.zh: 燧默然。

translations.literal: Sui fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Sui fell silent.

sentences.zh: 元諒請輸錢百萬勞軍自贖，瑊亦為請，燧赦之。

translations.literal: Yuanliang offered a million strings of cash to reward the army and redeem himself; Jian also pleaded for him, and Sui pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang offered a million strings of cash to reward the army and redeem himself. Jian also pleaded for him, and Sui pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 帝以專殺，恐有司劾治，前詔勿論。

translations.literal: Because he had killed on his own authority, the emperor feared the authorities would impeach him and issued a prior edict that the matter was not to be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had killed on his own authority, the emperor feared the authorities would impeach him and issued a prior edict that the matter was not to be pursued.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，吐蕃請盟，詔以軍從瑊會平涼，元諒軍潘原、遊瑰軍洛口以為援。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan Tibet requested alliance; an edict ordered troops to follow Jian to meet at Pingliang, with Yuanliang's army at Panyuan and Yougui's at Luokou as support.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyuan Tibet requested alliance. An edict ordered troops to follow Jian to meet at Pingliang, with Yuanliang's army at Panyuan and Yougui's at Luokou as support.

sentences.zh: 元諒曰：「潘原去平涼七十里，虜詐不情，如有急，何以赴？

translations.literal: Yuanliang said: "Panyuan is seventy li from Pingliang. The barbarians are treacherous — if there is an emergency, how can we respond?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang said, "Panyuan is seventy li from Pingliang. The barbarians are treacherous — if there is an emergency, how can we respond?

sentences.zh: 請與公連屯。」

translations.literal: I ask to camp jointly with you.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to camp jointly with you.

sentences.zh: 瑊以違詔，不聽。

translations.literal: Jian, saying it would violate the edict, did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, saying it would violate the edict, did not agree.

sentences.zh: 瑊壁盟所二十里，元諒密徙營次之。

translations.literal: Jian fortified twenty li from the alliance site; Yuanliang secretly moved his camp to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian fortified twenty li from the alliance site. Yuanliang secretly moved his camp to join him.

sentences.zh: 既會，元諒望雲物曰：「不詳，虜必有變！」

translations.literal: When they met, Yuanliang observed the clouds and omens and said: "This is ill-omened — the barbarians must be plotting something!
translations.idiomatic: When they met, Yuanliang observed the clouds and omens and said, "This is ill-omened — the barbarians must be plotting something!

sentences.zh: 傳令約部伍出陣。

translations.literal: He passed orders for the units to form battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: He passed orders for the units to form battle lines.

sentences.zh: 俄而虜劫盟，瑊奔還，元諒兵成列出，而涇原節度使李觀亦以精兵五千伏險，與元諒相表裏，虜騎乃解。

translations.literal: Soon the barbarians broke the alliance; Jian fled back, Yuanliang's troops deployed in full array, and Jingyuan military commissioner Li Guan also lay in ambush with five thousand elite troops, coordinating inside and out with Yuanliang, and the barbarian cavalry then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the barbarians broke the alliance. Jian fled back while Yuanliang's troops deployed in full array. Jingyuan military commissioner Li Guan also lay in ambush with five thousand elite troops, coordinating with Yuanliang inside and out, and the barbarian cavalry then dispersed.

sentences.zh: 元諒遣車重先，而與瑊振旅徐還，時以為有古良將風。

translations.literal: Yuanliang sent the baggage train ahead and withdrew slowly with Jian in good order; at the time he was thought to have the manner of the great generals of old.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang sent the baggage train ahead and withdrew slowly with Jian in good order. At the time he was thought to have the manner of the great generals of old.

sentences.zh: 是會也，微元諒、觀二人，瑊且不免。

translations.literal: At this meeting, but for Yuanliang and Guan the two of them, Jian would scarcely have escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At this meeting, but for Yuanliang and Guan, Jian would scarcely have escaped.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉嘆，賜善馬金幣良厚，因賜姓及名。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him with admiration and bestowed fine horses and gold and coins in great abundance, and thereby granted him the imperial surname and name.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him with admiration and bestowed fine horses, gold, and coins in great abundance, and thereby granted him the imperial surname and name.

sentences.zh: 更節度隴右，治良原。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as military commissioner of Longyou and governed at Liangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as military commissioner of Longyou and governed at Liangyuan.

sentences.zh: 良原隍堞湮圮，旁皆平林薦草，虜入寇，常牧馬休徒於此。

translations.literal: Liangyuan's moat and walls were sunken and ruined; all around were level woods and rank grass where barbarians on raids often pastured horses and rested their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyuan's moat and walls were sunken and ruined. All around were level woods and rank grass where barbarians on raids often pastured horses and rested their troops.

sentences.zh: 元諒培高浚淵，身執苦與士卒均，菑翳榛莽，辟美田數十里，勸士墾藝，歲入粟菽數十萬斛，什具畢給。

translations.literal: Yuanliang raised the heights and deepened the moats, himself took up hardship equal to the troops, cleared thorn and bramble, opened fine fields for several tens of li, urged the soldiers to reclaim and plant, and yearly harvests of grain and beans reached several hundred thousand hu; all equipment was fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang raised the heights and deepened the moats, himself sharing the soldiers' hardship, cleared thorn and bramble, opened fine fields for several tens of li, urged the soldiers to reclaim and plant, and yearly harvests of grain and beans reached several hundred thousand hu. All equipment was fully supplied.

sentences.zh: 又築連弩臺，遠烽偵，為守備，進據勢勝，列新壁。

translations.literal: He also built repeating-crossbow towers, extended beacon and scout lines, made defensive preparations, advanced to hold advantageous ground, and arrayed new walls.
translations.idiomatic: He also built repeating-crossbow towers, extended beacon and scout lines, made defensive preparations, advanced to hold advantageous ground, and arrayed new walls.

sentences.zh: 虜至無所掠，戰又輒北，由是涇、隴以安，西戎憚之。

translations.literal: When barbarians came there was nothing to plunder, and in battle they were repeatedly defeated; thereby Jing and Long were secured and the western barbarians feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When barbarians came there was nothing to plunder, and in battle they were repeatedly defeated. Thereby Jing and Long were secured and the western barbarians feared him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十二，贈司空，謚曰莊威。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-two and was posthumously made Minister of Works with the posthumous title Zhuangwei.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age sixty-two and was posthumously made Minister of Works with the posthumous title Zhuangwei.

sentences.zh: 李觀，其先自趙郡徙洛陽，故為洛陽人。

translations.literal: Li Guan — his ancestors had moved from Zhao commandery to Luoyang, so he was a man of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guan — his ancestors had moved from Zhao commandery to Luoyang, so he was counted a man of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 少沈厚寡言。

translations.literal: In youth he was deep, steady, and sparing of speech.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was deep, steady, and sparing of speech.

sentences.zh: 以策干朔方節度使郭子儀，子儀遣佐坊州刺史吳伷為防遏使。

translations.literal: He presented a policy memorial to Shuofang military commissioner Guo Ziyi; Ziyi sent him to assist Fangzhou prefect Wu Xian as defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He presented a policy memorial to Shuofang military commissioner Guo Ziyi. Ziyi sent him to assist Fangzhou prefect Wu Xian as defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以親喪解。

translations.literal: He resigned on account of a parent's death.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on account of a parent's death.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃內寇，代宗幸陜，觀隱盩厔，率鄉里子姓千人守黑水，虜不敢侵。

translations.literal: When Tibetans raided within the borders and Emperor Daizong went to Shan, Guan hid in Zhouzhi, led a thousand kinsmen of his district to hold Heishui, and the barbarians did not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans raided within the borders and Emperor Daizong went to Shan, Guan hid in Zhouzhi, led a thousand kinsmen of his district to hold Heishui, and the barbarians did not dare invade.

sentences.zh: 嶺南節度使楊慎微奏為偏將，徐浩、李勉代節度，常倚以軍政，數捕平劇賊。

translations.literal: Lingnan military commissioner Yang Shenwei memorialized him as a subordinate general; when Xu Hao and Li Mian succeeded as commissioners they often relied on him for military affairs and repeatedly captured and pacified fierce bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan military commissioner Yang Shenwei memorialized him as a subordinate general. When Xu Hao and Li Mian succeeded as commissioners they often relied on him for military affairs and repeatedly captured and pacified fierce bandits.

sentences.zh: 遷大將，試殿中監，召為右龍武將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to senior general, made acting Palace Director, and summoned as Right Dragon Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to senior general, made acting Palace Director, and summoned as Right Dragon Martial General.

sentences.zh: 涇師叛，觀適番上，即領兵千餘扈德宗奉天。

translations.literal: When the Jing army rebelled, Guan happened to be on palace duty and at once led more than a thousand troops to escort Dezong to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing army rebelled, Guan happened to be on palace duty and at once led more than a thousand troops to escort Dezong to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 詔盡察諸軍，整飭誰邏，增募五千人，鼙旝歡豎，士氣益振。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to inspect all armies, put patrols in order, recruit five thousand more men; drums and banners were raised in celebration and morale grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to inspect all armies, put patrols in order, and recruit five thousand more men. Drums and banners were raised in celebration and morale grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 賜封戶二百，授二子八品官。

translations.literal: He was granted a fief of two hundred households and eighth-rank offices for two sons.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a fief of two hundred households and eighth-rank offices for two sons.

sentences.zh: 從至梁州。

translations.literal: He followed to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝還，詔總後軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, an edict ordered him to command the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, an edict ordered him to command the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 擢四鎮、北庭行軍涇原節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military commissioner of Jingyuan for the Four Garrisons and Beiting campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to military commissioner of Jingyuan for the Four Garrisons and Beiting campaign.

sentences.zh: 在屯四年，訓部伍，儲藏饒衍。

translations.literal: At his garrison four years he trained the ranks and stores were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: At his garrison four years he trained the ranks and stores were abundant.

sentences.zh: 平涼之盟，吐蕃不得志。

translations.literal: At the Pingliang alliance Tibet did not achieve its aims.
translations.idiomatic: At the Pingliang alliance Tibet did not achieve its aims.

sentences.zh: 是年，觀入朝，前一日就道，虜至期出精騎狙擊，不及，去。

translations.literal: That year Guan went to court; he set out the day before, and the barbarians on schedule sent elite cavalry to ambush him but could not catch up and departed.
translations.idiomatic: That year Guan went to court. He set out the day before, and the barbarians on schedule sent elite cavalry to ambush him but could not catch up and departed.

sentences.zh: 以少府監檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was made acting Minister of Works with the rank of Director of the Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Minister of Works with the rank of Director of the Palace Workshops.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 韓遊瑰

translations.literal: Han Yougui
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui

sentences.zh: 韓遊瑰，靈州靈武人，始為郭子儀裨將。

translations.literal: Han Yougui was a native of Lingwu in Ling Prefecture and at first served Guo Ziyi as a subordinate general.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui was a native of Lingwu in Lingzhou and at first served Guo Ziyi as a subordinate general.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，使阿史那從禮將同羅、突厥五千騎偽降於朔方，出塞門，誘河曲九蕃府、六胡叛，部落凡五十萬。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he sent Ashina Congli with five thousand Tiele and Turk horsemen to feign surrender at Shuofang, exit the frontier pass, and entice the nine tribal offices and six Hu of Hequ to rebel — tribes totaling five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he sent Ashina Congli with five thousand Tiele and Turk horsemen to feign surrender at Shuofang, exit the frontier pass, and entice the nine tribal offices and six Hu of Hequ to rebel — tribes totaling five hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 子儀使遊瑰率辛京杲擊破之，九蕃府還附。

translations.literal: Ziyi sent Yougui leading Xin Jinggao to defeat them, and the nine tribal offices returned to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi sent Yougui leading Xin Jinggao to defeat them, and the nine tribal offices returned to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 累進邠寧節度留後。

translations.literal: He rose in stages to acting military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to acting military commissioner of Binning.

sentences.zh: 奉天之狩，兵未集，遊瑰與慶州刺史論惟明以兵三千來赴，自乾陵北趨醴泉，未至，有詔引軍屯便橋。

translations.literal: During the hunt at Fengtian the armies were not yet gathered; Yougui and Qingzhou prefect Lun Weiming came with three thousand troops, marching north of Qianling toward Liquan; before they arrived, an edict ordered the army to encamp at Bian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: During the withdrawal to Fengtian the armies were not yet gathered. Yougui and Qingzhou prefect Lun Weiming came with three thousand troops, marching north of Qianling toward Liquan. Before they arrived, an edict ordered the army to encamp at Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 次泥泉，與泚兵值，遊瑰欲還奉天，監軍翟文秀曰：「吾壁於此，賊敢逾我而西，可夾攻取之。

translations.literal: Halting at Niquan they met Zhu Ci's troops; Yougui wished to return to Fengtian. Army supervisor Zhai Wenxiu said: "If we fortify here, the rebels will not dare pass west of us — we can take them in a pincer.
translations.idiomatic: Halting at Niquan they met Zhu Ci's troops. Yougui wished to return to Fengtian. Army supervisor Zhai Wenxiu said, "If we fortify here, the rebels will not dare pass west of us — we can take them in a pincer.

sentences.zh: 今入奉天，賊亦隨至，是引賊迫天子也。」

translations.literal: If we now enter Fengtian, the rebels will follow — that is to lead the rebels upon the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If we now enter Fengtian, the rebels will follow — that is to lead the rebels upon the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰曰：「不然，我寡賊眾。

translations.literal: Yougui said: "Not so — we are few and the rebels many.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui said, "Not so — we are few and the rebels many.

sentences.zh: 彼分以亢我，餘眾猶能鼓而西也，不如先入衛天子。

translations.literal: If they divide to oppose us, the remainder can still drum westward. Better to enter first and guard the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If they divide to oppose us, the remainder can still drum westward. Better to enter first and guard the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 且奉天無強卒，安得夾攻？

translations.literal: Besides, Fengtian has no strong troops — how can there be a pincer attack?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Fengtian has no strong troops — how can there be a pincer attack?

sentences.zh: 吾士乏且寒，賊以利誘之，眾且潰。」

translations.literal: Our troops are weary and cold; the rebels will entice them with profit and the host will collapse."
translations.idiomatic: Our troops are weary and cold. The rebels will entice them with profit and the host will collapse."

sentences.zh: 遂還奉天。

translations.literal: Thereupon they returned to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they returned to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 泚兵躡攻之，戰不利；

translations.literal: Zhu Ci's troops pursued and attacked; the battle went badly;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci's troops pursued and attacked. The battle went badly;

sentences.zh: 泚兵奪門，遊瑰殊死戰，乃解。

translations.literal: the rebels seized the gate; Yougui fought to the death and the crisis was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: the rebels seized the gate. Yougui fought to the death and the crisis was relieved.

sentences.zh: 泚大治戰棚、雲橋，士皆懼，遊瑰曰：「賊取佛祠幹木為攻具，可以火之。」

translations.literal: Zhu Ci greatly prepared siege sheds and cloud bridges; the troops were all afraid. Yougui said: "The rebels take dry timber from Buddhist shrines for assault engines — they can be burned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci greatly prepared siege sheds and cloud bridges. The troops were all afraid. Yougui said, "The rebels take dry timber from Buddhist shrines for assault engines — they can be burned.

sentences.zh: 既而賊大噪攻南雉，遊瑰曰：「是分吾力也。」

translations.literal: Soon the rebels raised a great clamor attacking the southern bastion. Yougui said: "This is to divide our strength."
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels raised a great clamor attacking the southern bastion. Yougui said, "This is to divide our strength."

sentences.zh: 趨北雉，遣將郭詢、郭廷玉以銳士三百傅滿直出，火其棚，投薪於中，風返，棚皆燼，賊氣沮。

translations.literal: He hurried to the northern bastion, sent generals Guo Xun and Guo Tingyu with three hundred elite troops carrying full fuel bundles straight out, set fire to the sheds, cast fuel within; the wind reversed, the sheds were all consumed to ash, and rebel morale sank.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried to the northern bastion and sent generals Guo Xun and Guo Tingyu with three hundred elite troops carrying full fuel bundles straight out. They set fire to the sheds and cast fuel within. The wind reversed, the sheds were all consumed to ash, and rebel morale sank.

sentences.zh: 故諸將推遊瑰赴難功第一。

translations.literal: Therefore the generals ranked Yougui first in merit for going to the emperor's relief.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the generals ranked Yougui first in merit for going to the emperor's relief.

sentences.zh: 帝以衛軍無職局，軍置統軍一員，以遊瑰、惟明、賈隱林處之。

translations.literal: Because the guard armies lacked formal offices, the emperor established one army commander post each and placed Yougui, Weiming, and Jia Yinlin in them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the guard armies lacked formal offices, the emperor established one army commander post each and placed Yougui, Weiming, and Jia Yinlin in them.

sentences.zh: 李懷光叛，誘遊瑰為變，遊瑰白髮其書。

translations.literal: When Li Huai'guang rebelled he tried to entice Yougui into mutiny; Yougui reported the letter in full.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huai'guang rebelled he tried to entice Yougui into mutiny. Yougui reported the letter in full.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿可謂忠義矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You may truly be called loyal and righteous!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You may truly be called loyal and righteous!

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣安知忠義？

translations.literal: He replied: "How would your servant know loyalty and righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "How would your servant know loyalty and righteousness?

sentences.zh: 但懷光誤臣，使震驚乘輿，後持臣自解。」

translations.literal: Only Huai'guang misled your servant, making me alarm the imperial carriage; afterward he would hold your servant up to excuse himself."
translations.idiomatic: Only Huai'guang misled your servant, making me alarm the imperial carriage. Afterward he would hold your servant up to excuse himself."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其誠，從問：「計欲安出？」

translations.literal: The emperor praised his candor and then asked: "What plan do you propose?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his candor and then asked, "What plan do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「懷光總諸府兵，怙以為亂。

translations.literal: He replied: "Huai'guang commands the troops of all prefectures and relies on them to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Huai'guang commands the troops of all prefectures and relies on them to rebel.

sentences.zh: 今邠有張昕，靈武有寧薍景璿，河中有呂鳴嶽，振武有杜從政，潼關有李朝臣，渭北有竇覦，皆守將也。

translations.literal: Now Bin has Zhang Xin, Lingwu has Ning Zhi Jingxuan, Hezhong has Lü Mingyue, Zhenwu has Du Congzheng, Tong Pass has Li Chaochen, and north of the Wei has Dou Ni — all are garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Now Bin has Zhang Xin, Lingwu has Ning Zhi Jingxuan, Hezhong has Lü Mingyue, Zhenwu has Du Congzheng, Tong Pass has Li Chaochen, and north of the Wei has Dou Ni — all are garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 陛下以其眾與地授之，罷懷光權，而尊以元功，諸將仰首，各聽其帥，彼安能以亂？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should grant them the troops and territory, strip Huai'guang of power, and honor him with the title of founding merit. The generals will look up; each will obey his own commander — how could they rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should grant them the troops and territory, strip Huai'guang of power, and honor him with the title of founding merit. The generals will look up; each will obey his own commander — how could they rebel?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「罷懷光權而泚益張，若何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If we strip Huai'guang of power and Zhu Ci grows stronger, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If we strip Huai'guang of power and Zhu Ci grows stronger, what then?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下約士以不次之賞，今貢賦方至，發而酬之，其守自固。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty pledged extraordinary rewards to the troops. Tribute is now arriving — distribute it as payment and their garrisons will hold of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your Majesty pledged extraordinary rewards to the troops. Tribute is now arriving — distribute it as payment and their garrisons will hold of themselves.

sentences.zh: 邠有萬精甲，臣得將之，可以誅賊。

translations.literal: Bin has ten thousand elite armored troops; if your servant may lead them, the rebels can be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Bin has ten thousand elite armored troops. If your servant may lead them, the rebels can be executed.

sentences.zh: 四方杖義而起，賊不足慮。」

translations.literal: From all four directions men will rise up bearing the banner of righteousness; the rebels are scarcely worth worrying about."
translations.idiomatic: From all four directions men will rise up bearing the banner of righteousness. The rebels are scarcely worth worrying about."

sentences.zh: 帝美其言。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his words.

sentences.zh: 會懷光誘復至，渾瑊得書，稍嚴卒以警。

translations.literal: Just then Huai'guang's enticements arrived again; Hun Jian received a letter and tightened the guard on his troops somewhat as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Huai'guang's enticements arrived again. Hun Jian received a letter and tightened the guard on his troops somewhat as a warning.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰不知，發怒，嫚罵瑊。

translations.literal: Yougui did not know and flew into a rage, reviling and cursing Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui did not know and flew into a rage, reviling and cursing Jian.

sentences.zh: 帝疑有變，即日幸梁州，遊瑰使子從帝。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected trouble and that same day went in person to Liangzhou; Yougui had his son follow the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected trouble and that same day went in person to Liangzhou. Yougui had his son follow the emperor.

sentences.zh: 懷光檄假遊瑰邠州刺史，欲因張昕殺之。

translations.literal: Huai'guang issued an order appointing Yougui provisional governor of Bin Prefecture, intending to use Zhang Xin to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang issued an order appointing Yougui provisional governor of Bin Prefecture, intending to use Zhang Xin to kill him.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰既失兵，不知所圖。

translations.literal: Yougui had already lost his troops and did not know what to plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui had already lost his troops and did not know what to plan.

sentences.zh: 有客劉南金說曰：「邠有留甲，可以立功，殆天假也！」

translations.literal: A guest, Liu Nanjin, urged him: "At Bin there are troops still stationed — merit can be won there; perhaps Heaven is lending you the chance!
translations.idiomatic: A guest, Liu Nanjin, urged him, "At Bin there are troops still stationed. Merit can be won there — perhaps Heaven is lending you the chance!

sentences.zh: 遊瑰悟，誘舊部兵八百馳入邠，說昕曰：「懷光自蹈禍機，公今可取富貴，無共汙不義也。

translations.literal: Yougui understood. He lured eight hundred men of his old command and galloped into Bin, telling Xin: "Huai'guang has brought disaster on himself. You can seize wealth and rank now — do not join him in this unrighteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui understood. He lured eight hundred men of his old command and galloped into Bin, telling Xin, "Huai'guang has brought disaster on himself. You can seize wealth and rank now — do not join him in this unrighteousness.

sentences.zh: 我願以麾下為公先驅。」

translations.literal: I am willing to lead my troops ahead of you as your vanguard."
translations.idiomatic: I am willing to lead my troops ahead of you as your vanguard."

sentences.zh: 昕不聽。

translations.literal: Xin would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xin would not listen.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰移疾不出，陰結其將高固等。

translations.literal: Yougui feigned illness and did not go out, secretly winning over Xin's generals Gao Gu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui feigned illness and did not go out, secretly winning over Xin's generals Gao Gu and others.

sentences.zh: 昕欲殺遊瑰，戒左右衷甲入。

translations.literal: Xin wanted to kill Yougui and ordered his attendants to enter wearing armor beneath their robes.
translations.idiomatic: Xin wanted to kill Yougui and ordered his attendants to enter wearing armor beneath their robes.

sentences.zh: 昕小史李岌潛白遊瑰，伏甲先起，高固等應之，斬昕首以聞。

translations.literal: Xin's clerk Li Ji secretly informed Yougui; hidden soldiers rose first, Gao Gu and the others responded, and they beheaded Xin and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's clerk Li Ji secretly informed Yougui. Hidden soldiers rose first; Gao Gu and the others responded, and they beheaded Xin and reported it.

sentences.zh: 時懷光子玫在邠，遊瑰衛出之，曰：「殺之只以怒敵，至必遽，不如舍之。」

translations.literal: At the time Huai'guang's son Mei was at Bin; Yougui escorted him out and said: "Killing him would only enrage the enemy. When he arrives he will flee at once — better to let him go.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Huai'guang's son Mei was at Bin. Yougui escorted him out and said, "Killing him would only enrage the enemy. When he arrives he will flee at once — better to let him go.

sentences.zh: 玫至涇陽，懷光遂走蒲州。

translations.literal: Mei reached Jingyang, and Huai'guang then fled to Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mei reached Jingyang, and Huai'guang then fled to Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰屯七盤，受李晟節度。

translations.literal: Yougui encamped at Qipan and came under Li Sheng's command.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui encamped at Qipan and came under Li Sheng's command.

sentences.zh: 詔拜邠寧節度使，遂會渾瑊於奉天，與瑊、戴休顏分扼京西要險。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him military commissioner of Bin and Ning; he then joined Hun Jian at Fengtian and, with Jian and Dai Xiuyan, divided control of the strategic passes west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him military commissioner of Bin and Ning. He then joined Hun Jian at Fengtian and, with Jian and Dai Xiuyan, divided control of the strategic passes west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 李晟入長安，遊瑰破泚兵咸陽。

translations.literal: When Li Sheng entered Chang'an, Yougui defeated Zhu Ci's troops at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Sheng entered Chang'an, Yougui defeated Zhu Ci's troops at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 泚走涇州，遊瑰使諭涇將楊澄，澄拒不納，泚遂敗。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci fled to Jingzhou; Yougui sent envoys to persuade the Jing commander Yang Cheng, but Cheng refused to admit him, and Zhu Ci was thus defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci fled to Jingzhou. Yougui sent envoys to persuade the Jing commander Yang Cheng, but Cheng refused to admit him, and Zhu Ci was thus defeated.

sentences.zh: 京師平，遷檢校尚書左僕射，實封戶四百。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, he was promoted to honorary Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat with a substantive fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was pacified, he was promoted to honorary Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat with a substantive fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 帝至自興元，遊瑰及瑊、休顏從，而李晟、尚可孤、李元諒奉迎，論功與瑊等皆第一。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from Xingyuan, Yougui followed along with Jian and Xiuyan, while Li Sheng, Shang Ke'gu, and Li Yuanliang came out to welcome him; in reckoning merit, Yougui and Jian were ranked first alike.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Xingyuan, Yougui followed along with Jian and Xiuyan, while Li Sheng, Shang Ke'gu, and Li Yuanliang came out to welcome him. In reckoning merit, Yougui and Jian were ranked first alike.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰還屯邠寧。

translations.literal: Yougui returned to garrison Bin and Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui returned to garrison Bin and Ning.

sentences.zh: 懷光寇同州，瑊、元諒敗於乾坑。

translations.literal: Huai'guang raided Tongzhou; Jian and Yuanliang were defeated at Gankeng.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang raided Tongzhou. Jian and Yuanliang were defeated at Gankeng.

sentences.zh: 詔遊瑰率兵並力，敗賊眾五千於屯。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yougui to lead troops in a combined effort and defeat five thousand of the rebel host at Tun.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yougui to lead troops in a combined effort and defeat five thousand of the rebel host at Tun.

sentences.zh: 遂會瑊、馬燧圍蒲城。

translations.literal: He then joined Jian and Ma Sui in besieging Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Jian and Ma Sui in besieging Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 師次焦籬堡，守將尉珪降。

translations.literal: The army halted at Jiaoli Fort; the defending commander Wei Gui surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Jiaoli Fort. The defending commander Wei Gui surrendered.

sentences.zh: 懷光見勢單蹙，乃縊死。

translations.literal: Huai'guang saw that his force was isolated and hard-pressed and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang saw that his force was isolated and hard-pressed and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，吐蕃入涇、隴、邠、寧，遊瑰追至安化，虜營合水北。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, the Tibetans invaded Jing, Long, Bin, and Ning; Yougui pursued them to Anhua, and the barbarians camped north of the Heshui River.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyuan, the Tibetans invaded Jing, Long, Bin, and Ning. Yougui pursued them to Anhua, and the barbarians camped north of the Heshui River.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰策曰：「賊行無人地，必怠，可襲取之。」

translations.literal: Yougui devised a plan: "The enemy is marching through uninhabited country and will surely grow slack — we can take them by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui devised a plan: "The enemy is marching through uninhabited country and will surely grow slack. We can take them by surprise.

sentences.zh: 使將史履澄夜領兵五百入其營，斬數百級，取馬五千。

translations.literal: He had his general Shi Lucheng lead five hundred men by night into their camp, beheading several hundred and seizing five thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: He had his general Shi Lucheng lead five hundred men by night into their camp, beheading several hundred and seizing five thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 遲明，虜以兵尾擊，遊瑰羅幟自衛，鼙鼓四發，虜驚潰去。

translations.literal: At daybreak the barbarians struck from the rear; Yougui drew up his banners to protect himself, drums and gongs sounded on all sides, and the barbarians, startled, broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the barbarians struck from the rear. Yougui drew up his banners to protect himself; drums and gongs sounded on all sides, and the barbarians, startled, broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 是歲，復圍鹽州，刺史杜彥光約與之城，吐蕃許之，又取銀、夏、麟等州。

translations.literal: That year they again besieged Yanzhou; the prefect Du Yanguang agreed to hand over the city, the Tibetans accepted, and they also took Yin, Xia, Lin, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: That year they again besieged Yanzhou. The prefect Du Yanguang agreed to hand over the city; the Tibetans accepted and also took Yin, Xia, Lin, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰請收鹽州以斷戎人走集：「虜入漢，食禾菽，方春而病，此天亡時也。」

translations.literal: Yougui requested to recover Yanzhou and cut off the barbarians' routes of gathering and flight: "When the barbarians enter Han territory they eat our grain and beans; sick in early spring — this is Heaven's time to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui requested to recover Yanzhou and cut off the barbarians' routes of gathering and flight. He said, "When the barbarians enter Han territory they eat our grain and beans. Sick in early spring — this is Heaven's time to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 有詔李元諒、韓全義率師一萬，會遊瑰收鹽州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Li Yuanliang and Han Quanyi to lead ten thousand troops to join Yougui in recovering Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Li Yuanliang and Han Quanyi to lead ten thousand troops to join Yougui in recovering Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃請修清水盟，以歸侵地，馬燧為之請。

translations.literal: The Tibetans asked to renew the Qingshui covenant and return the invaded lands; Ma Sui pleaded on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans asked to renew the Qingshui covenant and return the invaded lands. Ma Sui pleaded on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 詔問遊瑰，答曰：「西戎弱則請盟，強則入寇。

translations.literal: The emperor inquired of Yougui, who replied: "When the western barbarians are weak they ask for a covenant; when they are strong they raid.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inquired of Yougui, who replied, "When the western barbarians are weak they ask for a covenant; when they are strong they raid.

sentences.zh: 今侵地益深而乞盟，詐我也！」

translations.literal: Now they have invaded deeper yet beg for alliance — they are deceiving us!
translations.idiomatic: Now they have invaded deeper yet beg for alliance — they are deceiving us!

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 會盟平涼，詔遊瑰以軍屯洛口。

translations.literal: At the covenant meeting at Pingliang, an edict had Yougui station his army at Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: At the covenant meeting at Pingliang, an edict had Yougui station his army at Luokou.

sentences.zh: 盟之日，遊瑰以勁騎五百待非常，令曰：「即有變，急趨柏泉以分虜勢。」

translations.literal: On the day of the covenant Yougui kept five hundred crack horsemen ready for the unexpected and ordered: "If trouble arises, hurry to Boquan to divide the barbarians' strength.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the covenant Yougui kept five hundred crack horsemen ready for the unexpected and ordered, "If trouble arises, hurry to Boquan to divide the barbarians' strength.

sentences.zh: 瑊被劫，馳以免，虜見兵出，即解去。

translations.literal: Jian was seized in an ambush but galloped free; when the barbarians saw troops coming out, they dispersed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was seized in an ambush but galloped free. When the barbarians saw troops coming out, they dispersed at once.

sentences.zh: 後吐蕃寇大回原，遊瑰方壁長武，即選騎八百迎擊，自引兵繼之。

translations.literal: Later the Tibetans raided the Dayuan plain; Yougui was fortifying Changwu and immediately selected eight hundred horsemen to meet the attack, personally leading the main force after them.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Tibetans raided the Dayuan plain. Yougui was fortifying Changwu and immediately selected eight hundred horsemen to meet the attack, personally leading the main force after them.

sentences.zh: 監軍以為戎不可易，答曰：「賊攻豐義，今遊騎先破，則彼大眾不敢前，豐義全矣！」

translations.literal: The army inspector thought the barbarians could not be lightly challenged; Yougui replied: "The enemy is attacking Fengyi. If our mobile cavalry breaks them first, their main body will not dare advance and Fengyi will be saved!
translations.idiomatic: The army inspector thought the barbarians could not be lightly challenged. Yougui replied, "The enemy is attacking Fengyi. If our mobile cavalry breaks them first, their main body will not dare advance and Fengyi will be saved!

sentences.zh: 戰南原，敗之，吐蕃夜遁。

translations.literal: They fought on the southern plain and defeated them; the Tibetans fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: They fought on the southern plain and defeated them. The Tibetans fled by night.

sentences.zh: 會子欽緒以射生將衛京師，與妖人李廣弘謀反，謀泄，奔邠州，中人捕斬，以狀示遊瑰。

translations.literal: Soon his son Qinxu, a shesheng officer guarding the capital, plotted rebellion with the sorcerer Li Guanghong; when the plot leaked, Qinxu fled to Binzhou, eunuchs captured and executed him, and showed the report to Yougui.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his son Qinxu, a shesheng officer guarding the capital, plotted rebellion with the sorcerer Li Guanghong. When the plot leaked, Qinxu fled to Binzhou. Eunuchs captured and executed him and showed the report to Yougui.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰懼，求歸死京師，帝不許。

translations.literal: Yougui was afraid and asked to return to the capital to accept death; the emperor refused.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui was afraid and asked to return to the capital to accept death. The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 又執欽緒二息送京師，帝亦原之。

translations.literal: He also seized Qinxu's two young sons and sent them to the capital; the emperor pardoned them as well.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized Qinxu's two young sons and sent them to the capital. The emperor pardoned them as well.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入朝，素服聽命，有詔復位，勞遇如故。

translations.literal: Before long he came to court, wearing plain dress to await orders; an edict restored him to his post and he was received with favors as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he came to court, wearing plain dress to await orders. An edict restored him to his post and he was received with favors as before.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰盛言城豐義以遏虜侵。

translations.literal: Yougui argued at length for building a fortress at Fengyi to block barbarian incursions.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui argued at length for building a fortress at Fengyi to block barbarian incursions.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，趣還軍。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and urged him to return to his army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and urged him to return to his army.

sentences.zh: 初，遊瑰之朝，眾謂且得罪，故賫送殊薄。

translations.literal: At first, when Yougui came to court, everyone expected he would be punished, so the gifts sent along were very meager.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Yougui came to court, everyone expected he would be punished, so the gifts sent along were very meager.

sentences.zh: 既還，舉軍不自安。

translations.literal: Once he returned, the whole army was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Once he returned, the whole army was ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 大將范希朝善兵，遊瑰畏其逼，欲誅之，希朝奔鳳翔，帝聞，召入宿衛。

translations.literal: The grand general Fan Xichao was skilled in warfare; Yougui feared his pressure and wanted to execute him; Xichao fled to Fengxiang, and when the emperor heard, he summoned Xichao into the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general Fan Xichao was skilled in warfare. Yougui feared his pressure and wanted to execute him. Xichao fled to Fengxiang, and when the emperor heard, he summoned Xichao into the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰遣兵築豐義，才二板而潰，寧卒數百大掠，遊瑰不能禁。

translations.literal: Yougui sent troops to build Fengyi; after only two courses of wall it collapsed, several hundred Ningzhou soldiers went on a great rampage, and Yougui could not restrain them.
